findings.title: Unguarded Optional.get() can now throw for federated users whose storage does not expose the credential via getCredentials()
findings.body: The bean now resolves the credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user), which looks at user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream() and then local storage, and immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get(). Before this PR recovery codes were always written to the local DB, so the Optional was effectively always present when this form was rendered. With this PR, a user storage that returns true from supportsCredentialType/updateCredential/isConfiguredFor for "recovery-authn-codes" but does not override CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials() (the default returns an empty stream) will make the authenticator consider the user configured (configuredFor() uses isConfiguredFor), yet getCredential() returns Optional.empty() and this constructor throws NoSuchElementException, producing a 500 on the recovery-code login page. Same problem if the storage's getCredentials() returns a CredentialModel whose credentialData is not the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel JSON (createFromCredentialModel / getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() will fail). The bean should handle an absent/invalid credential gracefully (e.g. fall back to not displaying a code number) instead of crashing.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes are pushed to user storage as an undocumented JSON blob in challengeResponse, changing behaviour for existing storage providers
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the plaintext generated codes as a JSON array and passes it as the challengeResponse of a UserCredentialModel of type "recovery-authn-codes" to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). This creates a new implicit SPI contract (storage must parse a JSON array of raw codes from CredentialInput.getChallengeResponse(), hash/store them, consume them in isValid(), and expose a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel-compatible model from getCredentials()) that is documented nowhere in the SPI or in this method's javadoc. It is also a behaviour change: prior to this PR recovery codes were always stored in Keycloak's DB regardless of the storage provider; now any existing CredentialInputUpdater whose supportsCredentialType() is permissive (e.g. returns true for unknown types) and whose updateCredential() returns true will silently swallow the codes, and the local fallback is skipped, leaving the user with codes that the storage cannot validate. The contract should be documented (SPI javadoc / release note) and the format of the challengeResponse made explicit.

findings.title: User label and generation timestamp are dropped on the user-storage path
findings.body: When the credential is handed to the user storage, only the type and the JSON list of codes are passed in the UserCredentialModel; credentialModel.getUserLabel() and the generatedAt timestamp (taken from the form and validated against the auth note in RecoveryAuthnCodesAction) are discarded. The storage has no way to receive them, so the label the user entered during setup is silently lost for federated users, while it is persisted for local users. Either pass this metadata (e.g. via the existing RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel JSON) or document that it is not supported for user storage.

findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById is called with the id of a federated credential
findings.body: optUserCredentialFound may now come from getFederatedCredentialsStream(). When such a federated model reports allCodesUsed(), the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). That method only removes credentials from local Keycloak storage, so for a federated credential it is a no-op (or passes a null id if the storage did not set one), and the exhausted credential remains in the user storage. The user does get CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES added, so re-setup overwrites it eventually, but isConfiguredFor() keeps returning true in between, and disableCredentialType() would be the appropriate call for the federated case.

findings.title: Test storage never consumes recovery codes and NPEs for unknown users in getCredentials()
findings.body: getCredentials() rebuilds a fresh RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the raw list on every call and isValid() only checks membership in that list, so codes are never marked as used: getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() always returns code #0 and any code can be replayed indefinitely. The new test testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin asserts exactly that code 0 is requested, so it passes only because of this simplification and does not exercise the realistic case where the storage advances the next code / exhausts the codes (the allCodesUsed() branch in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator is never reached for federated users). Additionally getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, unlike isConfiguredFor()/getDisableableCredentialTypesStream(), so it throws NPE if called for a user not present in the map.

findings.title: Recovery codes cannot be disabled/removed in the test storage
findings.body: supportsCredentialType(), updateCredential(), isConfiguredFor() and isValid() were extended for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE, but disableCredentialType() still only handles OTP and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() never reports the recovery-codes type. Consequently neither the admin REST disableCredentialType nor the account console removal path can remove recovery codes from this storage, and there is no test for removing/disabling recovery codes stored in user storage (the analogous OTP flows testOTPSetupThroughAdminRESTAndLogin / testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin exist but have no recovery-codes counterpart).

findings.title: Class javadoc claims 4.8.3 compatibility but the provider now depends on APIs that did not exist then
findings.body: The javadoc states this is a 'UserStorage implementation created in Keycloak 4.8.3' used for backwards compatibility testing and that future versions 'should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider'. This PR changes the provider to use RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, CredentialModel.setCredentialData(), CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials() and KeycloakModelUtils.generateId() on the OTP path, none of which existed in 4.8.3. Either the documentation should be updated to reflect that the provider is no longer a frozen 4.8.3 snapshot, or the recovery-code support should live in a separate test provider so the backwards-compatibility guarantee the test is meant to verify is not weakened.
